boundary.rationale: A pentagon ≈1.3 km²: the DN1 (Calea Bucureștilor) corridor through Otopeni town from Str. Zborului (S) to the Hilton Garden Inn / Bd. Aeroportului (N), plus the landside of the airport — access roads, departures ramp (bridge, layer 1), arrivals level, multi-storey car parks, the CFR Aeroport station and the Terminal Vioara; airside (aprons, runways) left as backdrop.

stops.building_osm: w771096082 (terminal "Plecări"); arrivals w771096081 ("Sosiri"); CFR station w813193384

door.street: departures ramp (OSM w180054678: tertiary, bridge=yes, layer=1, one-way northbound along the terminal front)
door.side: E side (terminal on the right when driving north)
door.note: In 2022 (chapter year) cars dropped off on this elevated kerb. Since 8 Dec 2025 cars may no longer stop on the Plecări lane because of the M6 "Aeroport Otopeni" metro works: drop-off moved to the car park in front of Departures; the Sosiri multi-storey car park (588 spaces) was closed for structural repairs and taxis/ride-hailing/buses moved to Plecări.

building.facade: long low terminal (2–3 storeys) with a full-height glass curtain wall facing landside, white/silver metal canopy over the kerb, big "Plecări / Departures" signs and the Bucharest Airports logo; Sosiri hall to the south is older/lower with a grey facade

stops.facts: Romania's busiest airport: just over 17 million passengers in 2025 (+6.6 %), 142,000 movements; a new 176,000 m² terminal (30 M pax/yr) is in design (2025–26); metro M6 Gara de Nord–Aeroport under construction since Dec 2023 (target 2028); CFR train link to "Aeroport Henri Coandă" station since 2020.
stops.cities_js_check: cities.js otopeni {44.5712, 26.0850} is ~600 m EAST of the terminal, airside on the apron. Landside departures kerb is at {44.5696, 26.0770}; terminal centroid {44.5713, 26.0775}.

top_local_details: DN1 is a dual carriageway with a central barrier, 70 km/h, flyover at the airport.
The departures kerb is ELEVATED (upper level), arrivals below.
OTP terminal = long glass front with a white canopy and "Plecări/Departures" signage.
Aircraft tails and the control tower visible beyond the terminal.
Yellow taxis and lots of ride-hailing cars at the kerb.
Express bus 100 / 780 (STB yellow) stops at the terminal.
CFR train station with covered walkway north-west of the terminal.
Multi-storey car parks opposite the terminal.
Since late 2024–25: M6 metro construction hoardings in front of Departures (not in 2022).
Hilton Garden Inn and Ibis Styles near the exit.
Fuel stations (OMV, Rompetrol) on DN1 in Otopeni.
Billboards on tall poles along DN1.
Flat, open landscape; few trees.
Security/police presence at the kerb; "Kiss & Go" style signs.
Planes landing/taking off on the two parallel 3,500 m runways 08R/26L and 08L/26R (OSM).
Novomatic HQ glass building on DN1.
Car dealerships lining DN1.
Wide shoulders and bus bays on DN1.
Overhead gantry direction signs (blue for DN, white for local) to "Aeroport Henri Coandă".
Speed cameras/radars on DN1 (local reputation).
Night: tall sodium/LED masts lighting the airport roads.
Rental-car lots and parking shuttles.
Departures hall glows at night through the glass.
TAROM office building near the access road.
Arrivals (Sosiri) hall older and lower than Departures.
Trolley-luggage crowds on the sidewalk.
Ilfov county (not Bucharest) — different street signs (blue "Otopeni" town signs).
Concrete Jersey barriers at the ramps.
Wizz Air pink/purple tails dominate the apron.
Gloria Jean's, Fornetti, Carrefour Express inside the terminal.

driving.note: RO:urban default 50; several boulevards signed 60 (OSM maxspeed=60 on Lascăr Catargiu, Magheru, Dorobanți north).

markings.lane_line: white dashed 3 m line / 6 m gap on urban roads (RO standard SR 1848-7), 0.10–0.15 m wide
markings.centre_line: white continuous (single) on 2-lane two-way, double continuous on 4+ lane two-way without median
markings.zebra: white bars 0.5 m wide / 0.5 m gap, parallel to traffic, no side lines; a few school-zone crossings have red infill between the white bars (verify per crossing on refs)
markings.bus_lane: white continuous line with "BUS" text; since 2019 some STB lanes on Magheru axis/Ștefan cel Mare painted red-brown (#9E3B2E) – verify per street
markings.yellow: yellow only for temporary works and kerb no-parking (zig-zag at bus stops)
markings.wear: markings visibly worn/faded on most streets except freshly resurfaced arteries — use 60–80% opacity

kerbs.material: grey concrete kerbstones 15×25 cm (older streets: granite #8C8C8C), kerb height 12–18 cm, often chipped

sidewalks.paving: mix: (a) grey concrete interlocking pavers ("pavele") #A9A59C on renovated boulevards; (b) cracked asphalt #6E6C68 on side streets; (c) 40×40 grey concrete slabs on 1960–80s estates
sidewalks.parking_on_sidewalk: very common: cars half/fully on the sidewalk on side streets, behind metal bollards on boulevards

traffic_lights.model: RO 3-aspect vehicle heads (200/300 mm), black or yellow housing with yellow-black backplates on main arteries, mounted on grey/black poles + overhead mast arms at big junctions; pedestrian 2-aspect (red/green man) with countdown displays on major junctions

street_name_plates.style: blue plate (#1F4E9A) white text "Bulevardul X" + sector number "Sector 1" in smaller text, on building corners or poles

bus_shelter.style: STB/Clear-channel style glass shelters with grey steel frame and backlit ad panel; many stops have only a pole with the yellow STB stop sign + timetable

metro_totem.style: Metrorex entrance: blue square sign with white "M", station name in white on blue; stairs down with grey stone/steel railings

trolleybus_wires.style: pair of copper contact wires 0.6 m apart per direction at ~5.6 m, carried by span wires between steel or concrete poles on both kerbs (often shared with street lamps)

tram_track.style: standard gauge 1435 mm; on boulevards in a central reservation with concrete sleepers/ballast or grass, kerbed and fenced in places; overhead single contact wire on span wires
